items.title: 68146_Russell Procope oral history interview
items.q: I remember that it was a real honor to me, to meet Donald Redman

ctx.x: Within a few blocks of each other. Everybody lived around the corner and down here and you'd bump into each other, you know, so I got to know all the musicians, not real well, some of them. It was -- and I remember that it was a real honor to me, to meet Donald Redman, even moreso than Fletcher Henderson, because he was such a great musician. Oh, he could play trumpet, piano, clarinet, saxophone, and one of the greatest arrangers, you know. That type of man is just a wonderful, talented person, and I thought a…

The way he hired me, he -- I don't remember exactly how -- I just don't remember the point when he -- when he offered me the job, but this was a period where I call it the Big Trade. items.title: 68146_Russell Procope oral history interview
items.q: He had Don Redman in the band and Don Redman was making all these beautiful arrangements.

ctx.x: He was among the first, wasn't he, to get away from the stock? Wasn't that what really separated him in the beginning from other bands?
Yes, he was the first. I would say yes, that he was the first to play manuscripts, you know. Special arrangements, we used to call them. Because don't forget that he had Don Redman in the band.
